stops.note: named horned beetles and crayfish; Aristotle's History of Animals uses it for the spiny lobster
Isidore of Seville's Etymologiae defines carabus as a small boat of wicker covered in raw hide
Portugal's light, lateen-rigged ship of discovery; Bartolomeu Dias rounded the Cape of Good Hope in 1488 with two caravels
came via French caravelle; two of Columbus's three ships in 1492, the Niña and the Pinta, were caravels

current_meaning: a small, fast Spanish or Portuguese sailing ship of the 1400s-1600s
